Process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_GZIP_ENABLED and FERRUM_COMPRESSION_BROTLI_ENABLED gates intersect with every instance and default to true; an instance with no remaining usable algorithm after those gates fails admission. Gzip/Brotli codec CPU is offloaded via a bounded spawn_blocking admission pool; authenticated /metrics exports ferrum_compression_codec_{admitted,saturated,join_failures,worker_failures}_total. Encode abort after a committed Content-Encoding restores identity headers on shared buffered H1/H2/H3 paths rather than emitting mislabeled plaintext. Optional request decompression parses Content-Encoding as an ordered coding list (OWS-tolerant), decodes supported chains in reverse order under hard-capped size/amplification limits, and fails closed on malformed/unsupported members. Content negotiation follows RFC 9110 §12.5.3, treats x-gzip as the gzip compatibility token, strictly parses qvalues, and includes the identity coding: an uncoded response is acceptable by default at q=1 unless refused with `identity;q=0` or `*;q=0` without a more-specific identity entry (a nonzero wildcard does not lower identity quality), the most preferred acceptable representation wins (server preference order breaks ties toward compression), and the response is rejected with 406 when identity is unacceptable and no acceptable coded representation can be produced — including size/content-type ineligibility, identity range/delta responses (206/226, Content-Range, or the internal range marker), and `response_caching` HIT paths. Identity range/delta responses are non-transformable (forwarded unchanged when identity is acceptable); no-body statuses and already-encoded upstream responses remain protocol hard skips. Reject-path 406 replacement is scoped to cache HITs so auth/policy rejection statuses are not masked. Honors request/response Cache-Control: no-transform and strong ETag validators by skipping compression (still 406 when that leaves no acceptable representation). Siblings must not delete the owner's request marker or compress again. An earlier identity/Vary-only decision does not block a later compress.
